findings.title: Revoked legacy PAT can pass cached knowledge final-send authorization
findings.trigger: Legacy PAT resolver SELECT completes before revoke commit; its cache Set happens after the post-commit eviction, or eviction/commit acknowledgement fails. The account and membership remain active.
findings.impact: Queued or subsequent knowledge hints reveal target identity/revision through a credential already revoked in PostgreSQL for up to the cache TTL.
findings.minimal_fix: Give only the knowledge final-send path the original trusted credential identity and perform uncached database PAT revoked/expiry/user validation alongside existing JWT/password and human/member checks. Preserve unrelated realtime behavior.
findings.regression: Actual queued knowledge frame; active member; commit PAT revoke; stale cache resolver still returns user; no knowledge frame is sent. Include valid-PAT and password/JWT controls.

findings.title: Knowledge final-send validator forwards unchecked envelope fields
findings.trigger: A knowledge frame has a valid last payload plus an outer private field, or duplicate payload with existing event_id. The permissive envelope decoder ignores data which the raw-byte send retains.
findings.impact: The promised malformed/private-frame denial and content-free final-send boundary are not enforced outside the current safe typed producer.
findings.minimal_fix: Strictly allow only type, validated payload and optional valid event_id for knowledge frames, reject duplicate/extra data or construct canonical bytes from validated values, and fail closed for known malformed knowledge frames without changing ordinary events.
findings.regression: Reject outer source_id and duplicate private payload plus event_id; preserve valid exact payload and retained deleted-project delivery.
findings.limitation: The F3 drainer itself currently emits a safe typed envelope; this is a final-boundary correctness finding.

limitations: A2 human API/resolver and C2 execution work are separate unfinished batches and were not judged as F3 failures.
No live browser/desktop acceptance, provider-session proof or whole-task completion is claimed.
The Core 30-second lease and 15-second reread are fallback behavior, not server authorization evidence.
